newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cardoso's help sought over Patricia coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cardoso's help sought over Patricia coffee.

text.p: Brazil's Coffee Exporters' Federation (Febec) has sent letter to the country's president to request he find a way to resolve debt problems linked to the so-called "Operation Patricia", Febec said.

"Operation Patricia" involved 18 companies which, acting for the now-defunct Brazilian Coffee Institute (IBC), bought a total of 635,000 60-kg bags of coffee on the London exchange in August 1986, Febec said on a statement.
The idea was to maximize Brazil's revenue from its coffee exports which were sharply down that year because of a drought.
Trade houses were to buy futures contracts, take delivery of coffee and then in theory were to be paid back either in coffee or in cash.
However since 1987, the companies have only received $15 million, around one tenth of what they are owed.
In April 1990, four companies won a judgement against the IBC in the UK High Court which ordered the IBC to compensate the four firms.
The same year the IBC was liquidated, with the Brazilian government assuming all outstanding obligations.
Most recently a sequestration order was served on the Milan branch of Germany's Deutsche Bank ordering the seizure of Brazilian government assets following the issue of a 500 billion lire bond.
All monies from the bond have arrived in Brazil however without interference, Central Bank officials have said.
There have also been suggestions that concerns over the legal situation delayed the announcement of a 150-million sterling 10-year Eurobond.
Central Bank officials have however said that any delay was to allow time to evaluate a recent rise in the official British interest rate. The bond was announced on July 14.
